topic: Blockbuster turned down a deal to buy Netflix, laughed it off, then watched Netflix beat it
title: Blockbuster Laughed at the $50 Million Netflix Deal
note: Gemini first draft, NOT fact-checked. Claude must verify every claim with its own 2-source rule before using any of it in a real job file.
draft_outline: By 2010, Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy. Netflix market cap reached $2.5 billion.
In 2000, Blockbuster operated 9,000 stores. Netflix reported 300,000 subscribers and $5 million annual loss.
In September 2000, Netflix offered Blockbuster a 49% stake for $50 million. Blockbuster declined.
Netflix pivoted to online streaming in 2007. Blockbuster attempted Blockbuster Total Access in 2004, then Blockbuster On Demand in 2007.
By 2010, Netflix had 16 million subscribers. Blockbuster had 1,700 remaining stores. By 2011, Netflix market cap exceeded $11 billion. Blockbuster liquidated assets.
Market leadership is temporary. Ignoring disruptive innovation carries high cost.
